summary: CCC built a fire tower on Roan High Knob in 1933; the register lists it removed and lookout footings remain. The 1980 cabin became an AT shelter, closed since 2024.

facts.status_note: Tennessee's register lists the tower as removed. The cabin built with it became a trail shelter, closed since September 2024.

access.note: The summit is reached by a blue-blazed side trail off the Appalachian Trail. Hikers are asked to avoid the closed shelter area.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The shelter is closed; the summit is a short blue-blazed side trail off the Appalachian Trail.

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps built a fire tower and a fire warden's cabin on Roan High Knob
The cabin was renovated and became the Roan High Knob Shelter for Appalachian Trail hikers
The shelter was closed for structural concerns

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb and Wikipedia date the CCC-built tower and cabin to 1933. The Tennessee Eastman Hiking and Canoeing Club wiki dates the cabin to 1934 and credits the Forest Service. The story uses 1933 and reports the wiki's date.
WillhiteWeb places the cabin at the base of the tower; Wikipedia places it at the summit. The story says only that both stood on Roan High Knob.

The Appalachian Trail Conservancy's September 2025 update says the shelter remained closed with no timeline for reopening. The Forest Service project page lists a repair project as completed, with a decision dated 29 April 2025. The story gives both.
WillhiteWeb gives a 0.2-mile detour; the Tennessee Eastman Hiking and Canoeing Club wiki gives 0.1 mile. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: No source gives the tower's removal date or who removed it; 'removed' rests on the tnlandforms register alone. The built-date and cabin-location conflicts and the shelter-status conflict are in resolved_conflicts. The shelter status may have changed after the September 2025 Appalachian Trail Conservancy update; recheck that page before publishing. The photo caption 'Fire lookout footing' is the only evidence of remains. Brief agency (Cherokee National Forest) confirmed by the Forest Service page and the register.
